answer: Each identity roots its signing key in a one-time remote attestation of a unique enclave measurement, recorded in a public atlas that rejects any duplicate root. The vine of usable tenure grows only from that attested silicon, as hard to clone as a karst cave system formed in unique geology. An attacker who wants 350 aliases must therefore buy and provision 350 separate physical chips, while an honest agent pays for one device once. If the atlas check is skipped, the vine accepts shared clones and the cost collapses.
